verdict.reasoning: REFUTED — pure leading-whitespace / page-break furniture, with zero content difference. (1) Text is complete and verbatim. I rendered spec_p961.png at 300 dpi and read every printed line. The page contains exactly six blocks: items 5. and 6., 'c) Otherwise,', '(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1).', the 'NOTE These errors include, but are not limited to:' lead-in, and three dashed bullets ('argument-1 is zero-length,' / 'argument-1 contains only spaces,' / "argument-1 contains valid characters but is incomplete, such as the string ' +.'."). Every one of these is present in specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 38455-38473, word for word, in the same order. Nothing is missing, nothing is added, nothing is reordered, and no wording differs. The claim itself alleges no textual difference — its own pdf_says and markdown_says quote identical prose. (2) The hierarchy is not lost, because the ordinal labels that encode it survive intact. The markdown keeps the literal tokens '5.', '6.' and 'c)'. Page 960 ends with items '1.' through '4.' nested under 'b)', preceded by 'a)' and 'b)' under '1) The returned value is:'. A reader of the assembled markdown can only parse '5.'/'6.' as the continuation of 1.-4., and 'c)' as the successor to a)/b). No rule can be misattributed to the wrong parent, and no returned-value semantics change. Note also that a)/b) on page 960 are likewise not markdown list markers — they are paragraph text — so 'c)' at column 0 is not being demoted from a real list level to a fake one; it was never a markdown list item. (3) The behavior is systemic transcription convention, not a page-961 defect. I scanned all 1233 page blocks: 323 of them (26%) begin with a bare list marker at column 0 immediately after the page heading, i.e. the pipeline drops the enclosing indent context at every page boundary by design. Flagging page 961 individually is noise against a documented, uniform artifact of page-segmented transcription. (4) The claim's implied remedy would make the file worse, so the current form is the defensible one. The transcription inserts '', '## Page 961' and the running header between page 960's list and this continuation. An ATX heading terminates any list in CommonMark, so re-indenting '5.' by six spaces would NOT restore list continuity — after a heading and a blank line, six leading spaces open an indented code block, rendering the two returned-value rules as monospaced code. Column 0 is the only form that renders as prose. (5) The kind label is inaccurate on its own terms. 'misplaced-content' asserts content sitting in the wrong place; here the content sits in exactly the right place, in the right sequence, under the right ordinals, and differs only in leading spaces. This falls squarely under the rejection criteria 'the difference is only page-break furniture ... or formatting' and 'the difference does not change meaning'.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. All of page 961's text — items 5. and 6., 'c) Otherwise,', '(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1).', the NOTE and its three dashed bullets — is transcribed completely and verbatim in the correct order at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:38455-38473. The sole difference is leading indentation: the PDF prints 5./6. one level deeper than c), while the markdown starts all three at column 0. That indent is dropped at every page boundary by the page-segmented transcription pipeline (323 of 1233 pages exhibit it), the nesting remains unambiguous from the surviving '5.'/'6.'/'c)' ordinals against page 960's 1.-4. and a)/b), and re-adding a six-space indent after the intervening '## Page 961' heading would render the text as an indented code block rather than restoring the list. No meaning is affected; no ledger entry warranted.
